cells.tense: The spark is here now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take a version you already picked and keep it going seven more days, doubt included, no sign needed to start. Then see what is still yours.
cells.core:
Something in you lights up before it has a shape. Where fairness is kept and things are set right, you are holding this well: the interest is fresh, the whole of you is present, and you have not voted yourself out while it burns. Nothing gets written off early here just because it has no track record yet. A beginning is allowed to be unproven.

Carry the version you chose through doubt for a while longer. You will not get a sign first. Ending the stretch with it still yours, even unwatched, is the whole of it. What held while nothing confirmed it is what can be trusted later.
cells.sheetLine: A beginning stays alive through the doubt that tests it.
cells.verb: lighting before you know what it is for
cells.place: where fairness is kept and things are set right

cells.tense: You are bracing for the correction before the ink has dried.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread every piece of what you are starting across a table, all of it visible together. Look, then walk away. Not one piece gets adjusted tonight.
cells.core:
Things catch fire in you fast, and where fairness is kept, the whole of it gets judged before it has drawn breath — every angle checked, every wrong turning anticipated, the correction ready before the beginning has had a day. It is not patience you are short of. It is room for something to be unproven. Fairness gets used like a verdict here, and a verdict before the fact is a strike ahead of time.

So spread the whole start across one surface, every piece visible at once, and walk away from it. Do not smooth a single line. What sits there is a whole thing in its early state, and it can stay that way while you look. Nothing has to come out even yet.

cells.tense: The door is one you already walked past without noticing it.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Put everything you feel about this start on a single sheet — all of it, nothing crossed out. Read it once, then stop. No verdict follows.
cells.core:
Beginnings are not catching in this stretch. You can watch something start, weigh it, look right past it — the door is not slammed, it is not noticed. You arrive after the moment, not in it, and the spark finds no purchase. It is not that you object to the starting. You are still with the last question.

Before you weigh anything, feel the whole of it. Everything you feel about this one start goes onto a single sheet — all of it, nothing crossed out — and you read it once. Not to decide. The felt thing arrives before the fair thing does; let it land first, or the scale tips without you on it.

cells.tense: The sparks you are already acting on sit in your ledger as luck.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Take a start already in motion and enjoy it for half an hour. No fixing, no next move queued up, no improving. Sign your name to it.
cells.core:
You start things where fairness is kept and things are set right, and going well, that is visible: a beginning catches, and you are in it without having to argue for it. What happens instead is quieter. The spark that begins is yours, and the ledger has it listed under circumstance, under timing, under somebody else's idea — the author's name is off the work.

Enjoy a start you already made. Nothing to fix, nothing next in line. For half an hour it is simply what it is, and you are the one who put it there. When that counts as yours, you will see your hand in the starts already under way.
cells.sheetLine: You make the starts. Your ledger credits luck.
